title: Frederick G. Williams joins the United Firm as a lively member
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, on 15 March 1833. A week earlier, Frederick G. Williams had been named to the presidency with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon. He had worked for the United Firm as a paid assistant scribe since January. The firm managed the church’s printing, stores, and properties in Kirtland and Missouri.
summary: The revelation is addressed to the united order, also called the United Firm. It tells the members to receive Frederick G. Williams into the order. It adds that what is said to one is said to all. Then it speaks to Williams himself. He is to be “a lively member” of the order. If he keeps all former commandments, he will be blessed forever.

contextNote.title: What a lively member owes
contextNote.text: Williams already served the firm, but only as a paid scribe. Verse 1 changes his standing by receiving him into the order itself. The JSP notes that firm members were to be equal partners with equal claims on its property. Verse 2 then asks him to be “a lively member,” an active partner rather than a name on a list. The promise in verse 2 depends on faithfulness to “all former commandments”. Here, lively means engaged and faithful in the firm’s shared work.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 89–92 includes this call to Frederick G. Williams. Verse 1 says what is said to one is said to all; what would being “a lively member” look like in your ward?
reviewNote: Read both verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 15 March 1833, to Frederick G. Williams about the United Firm. JSP introduction read for his role as assistant scribe since January 1833, the firm’s duties, and the equality of members. Williams was the first member added after the firm was organized. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
